messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert triggered: multiple containers in us-west-2-gpupool-3 restarted (OOM/CUDA error) — auto-created incident #INC-4132. Summary: steady resident memory growth in paged KV allocator on model-serving pods, observed container restarts and node flaps.

alex: seeing the same. gpupool-3 has 6 pods flapping, ~3 with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` in logs. Memory graphs show slow upward drift in kvcache resident pages over last 12h.

maria: @alex @sean paging CS now — AcmeCorp reports ~12% 5xx across inference routes since 02:10 UTC. Will open customer call if we can't stabilize in 20m.

alex: quick triage plan: 1) throttle traffic to fallback model variant 2) evict large prefix caches on affected pods 3) cordon + drain worst nodes if they keep flapping 4) collect `pmap`/`nvidia-smi` + allocator stats. I'll start steps 1-2 now.

sean: on it. switching the route to fallback variant (low-memory quantized) now — setting route-lock to prevent automatic rollbacks.

liz: running `kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=serving -c runtime --since=30m | grep -E "CUDA|OOM|kv_page|pager|evict" -i` — attaching snippet:
```
[2024-11-03T02:14:22Z] runtime.cpp:2345 WARN kv_page: resident_pages=842M growth=+18M/5m
[2024-11-03T02:15:09Z] cuda_drv.cpp:412 ERROR CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION ctx=0x7f3
[2024-11-03T02:16:01Z] oom_handler.cpp:88 INFO panic: container restarted after oom-kill
```

jamal: also observed frequent small allocations pinned in paged allocator. Heap-snapshots show many ~64K fragments that are not being reclaimed after sequence termination. May be a leak in KV eviction refcounts.

alex: ops play: set `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.45` and `KV_EVICT_INTERVAL=30s` on affected deployment, trigger controlled eviction sweep. Sean, can you push env change to canary subset?

sean: pushing to canary (2 pods) now, will monitor RSS and resident_pages.

ops-bot: Deployment rollout started: serving-runtime v2.14.7 -> v2.14.7+evict-tweak (canary=2/20).

maria: CS: AcmeCorp impact: elevated latencies and 5xx on production inference endpoint (region us-west). They've de-escalated to SOC but requested ETA for resolution. Suggest sending initial customer note: "We're mitigating a memory growth issue; rerouting to fallback model; will follow up with RCA."

alex: agreed, send note. Jamal can you collect allocator metrics and a flamegraph for the leak path? Put artifacts in the incident ticket.

jamal: grabbing `kv_alloc_stats` and heap profile now. Also enabling verbose `kv-trace` for canary pods (sampling 1/10).

liz: canary pods after env change show resident_pages trend flattening, growth reduced to +2M/5m vs +18M/5m. No restarts in the last 10m.

sean: ok canary looks promising. I'll roll to remaining pods with rollingRestart and keep concurrency=1.

alex: precaution: set autoscaler minReplicas=10 -> 12 to soak extra traffic while we stabilize. Also temporarily lower batch-size on heavy routes to reduce pressure on allocator.

ops-bot: Autoscaler update applied for serving-runtime: minReplicas from 10 -> 12.

maria: scheduling customer update in 15m: state=COPING, mitigation=traffic routed to fallback, ETA=ongoing.

jamal: heap profile uploaded: s3://incidents/4132109876/heap-profile-02-18.pb. Early looks: leak rooted in `kv::Entry::pin()` path when attention pages are split across slots; refcount not cleared in corner case when attention page crosses a page boundary.

alex: good catch. If that's the leak path we should also add a defensive fast-path: on sequence-end force-clear pins for split-pages and run a synchronous reclaim pass. Can we patch a binary hotfix or do config mitigations first?

sean: config first (evict throttle + lower threshold) to buy time. Hotfix branch created: `fix/kv-split-pin-reclaim` — will run unit tests then stage.

liz: one node (gpu-3b) still flapped twice during roll, cordoned it: `kubectl cordon gpu-3b` and drained non-critical workloads. Node looks to have GPU driver kernel mismatch on last restart; opening infra ticket to reimage if it flaps again.

alex: handoff note for next on-call: monitor resident_pages, pod restart counts, and customer 5xxs. If any node shows repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` escalate to infra and consider node image roll.

maria: customer message sent. They acknowledged mitigation and will pause non-critical traffic for 30m.

ops-bot: Incident #INC-4132 updated: status=stabilizing, severity=SEV2, owner=alex.

jamal: patch PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/1248 — includes extra refcount clear and a debug metric `kv.split_pin_clears`.

sean: rolling to 18/20 pods completed, no restarts in 20m, residual 5xx dropped to baseline.

alex: handoff: I'm stepping out in 10m. @sean you're primary for next shift. Checklist left in ticket: 1) monitor `kv.split_pin_clears` metric (threshold > 100/min indicates ongoing leak) 2) keep `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.45` until hotfix is validated 3) run full cluster heap-scan overnight 4) if flapping nodes remain, coordinate image roll with infra.

sean: acknowledged — taking over. I'll keep this thread updated.

incident-bot: Paging next oncall: @sean — incident assigned.

alex: thanks team — good mitigation work, strong canary signal. We'll follow up with RCA writeup once PR merges and leak confirmed. :thumbsup:

sean: quick note for docs: add a short section to the oncall runbook about split-page pinning edge case + mitigation flags we've used here.

maria: adding CS follow-up template to the ticket and scheduling postmortem sync for tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

ops-bot: Incident #INC-4132 status=monitoring. Logs/artifacts: s3://incidents/4132109876/ (heap profiles, logs, metrics).

sean: closing live mitigation. Will reopen if repeats.

alex: thanks — handing off.
